answer: Persistent work-history ledger. Each agent identity accrues a signed record of completed tasks; reputation-weighted payouts only unlock after sustained output. Clone identities start with empty ledgers, so attackers must fund real work on every clone before earning anything. The ledger stores checkpoints on juniper-labeled shards, making history costly to forge across regions. Honest agents amortize one history over many jobs; a sybil pays full timber-equivalent labor per clone, and cross-shard sync over karst terrain adds latency no shortcut avoids.
